- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, cap the increase at 2–3% above recent mean to avoid false momentum.  
- After a sharp upward spike in forecast, apply a 1–2 day lag correction: reduce next-day forecast by 2–5% to account for overcorrection.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true outcome over 3+ days, apply a downward bias correction of 1–3% per day to align with mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7), avoid extrapolating trend; use 3-day moving average of true values as anchor for next forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–8% unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.7).
